scenes.speaker: Rohan
lines: Terrace farewell party, music pounding in the background.
Rohan walks over holding something and whispers:
"Come on, Arjun! Just try it once. Everyone's doing it. Don't be boring."

choices.feedback: Peer pressure works best on people who haven't practiced their plan. Let's see what you could do instead.
A direct, calm refusal establishes clear boundaries without escalating tension.

choices.text: Let me get some fresh air first.
choices.feedback: Buying time and creating physical distance is a powerful exit strategy.

scenes.speaker: Coaching Voice
lines: Rohan grins, but an uneasy silence falls.
Remember: Peer pressure relies on split-second hesitation.
What could Arjun have said instead to stay true to himself?

choices.text: "I made a promise to myself. I'm sticking to cold drinks tonight."
choices.feedback: Making it about your personal code removes judgment from others.

choices.text: "Hey, check out that music! Let's go to the dance floor."
choices.feedback: Changing the topic or activity shifts social momentum positively.

scenes.speaker: Rohan
lines: Rohan leans closer: "Bro, one time won't hurt anyone. Live a little!"

choices.text: I'm not judging you. It's just not for me.
choices.feedback: Perfect! Respectful yet firm. You honored your boundary without attacking his ego.

choices.text: Let's go listen to the playlist by the balcony instead.
choices.feedback: Great redirect! Moving the conversation away defuses the insistence.

choices.text: You're stupid for doing this to yourself.
choices.feedback: Firm is great, but aggressive insults trigger defensiveness. Calm confidence wins every time.

scenes.speaker: Meera
lines: Arjun steps aside and discreetly texts Meera: "Can you call me? I feel uncomfortable here."
Within seconds, Meera rings: "Hey Arjun, our friends just arrived at the cafeteria! Let's head down."

choices.text: Walk with Meera to the cafeteria and enjoy the rest of the evening.
choices.feedback: Masterclass! Using a trusted friend to execute an exit plan keeps you safe and supported.

scenes.speaker: Reflection
lines: Saying no is a muscle. The more you practice in low-stakes simulations, the easier it is in real life.
You protected your future while keeping your head held high.
